37212-the-discards.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. by the robber speculator, land thief and all round crooks who swarm the reservations; as well as creating a deeper sentiment of respect for the Red race by giving first hand the Indian side of life; his poetry, music, philosophy and tribal history.

arxiv-2101-07503.title: Band Structure Dependent Electronic Localization in Macroscopic Films of Single-Chirality Single-Wall Carbon Nanotubes Journal: Carbon
arxiv-2101-07503.creator: Weilu Gao, Davoud Adinehloo, Xinwei Li, Ali Mojibpour, Yohei Yomogida, Atsushi Hirano, Takeshi Tanaka, Hiromichi Kataura, Ming Zheng, Vasili Perebeinos, Junichiro Kono
arxiv-2101-07503.description: Abstract Significant understanding has been achieved over the last few decades regarding chirality-dependent properties of single-wall carbon nanotubes (SWCNTs), primarily through single-tube studies. However, macroscopic manifestations of chirality dependence have been limited, especially in electronic transport, despite the fact that such distinct behaviors are needed for many applications of SWCNT-based devices.

arxiv-2105-04713.title: Lessons Learned from Virtual Transitions of Undergraduate Student Support Programs due to the COVID-19 Pandemic
arxiv-2105-04713.creator: Tierra Candelaria, Qiana Hunt, Danielle Rowland
arxiv-2105-04713.description: Abstract The COVID-19 global pandemic spurred sudden and dramatic changes in the way universities and research programs operate, often with negative consequences that have disproportionately affected minorities, women, and people with low income. These consequences compound the difficulties these groups faced prior to the pandemic — in particular, the increased obstacles marginalized students encounter while pursuing STEM career paths.

arxiv-2108-05346.title: Quantum microscopy based on Hong-Ou-Mandel interference
arxiv-2108-05346.creator: Bienvenu Ndagano, Hugo Defienne, Dominic Branford, Yash D. Shah, Ashley Lyons, Niclas Westerberg, Erik M. Gauger, Daniele Faccio
arxiv-2108-05346.description: Abstract Hong-Ou-Mandel (HOM) interference, the bunching of indistinguishable photons at a beam splitter, is a staple of quantum optics and lies at the heart of many quantum sensing approaches and recent optical quantum computers. Here, we report a full-field, scan-free, quantum imaging technique that exploits HOM interference to reconstruct the surface depth profile of transparent samples.

arxiv-2112-14086.title: Many faces of accretion in gamma ray bursts
arxiv-2112-14086.creator: Agnieszka Janiuk
arxiv-2112-14086.description: Abstract Accretion powers relativistic jets in GRBs, similarly to other jet sources. Black holes that are at heart of long GRBs, are formed as the end product of stellar evolution. At birth, some of the black holes must be very rapidly spinning, to be able to power the GRBS.

arxiv-2201-02468.title: Reply to the Comment on “Thermal, quantum antibunching and lasing thresholds from single emitters to macroscopic devices”
arxiv-2201-02468.creator: Mark Anthony Carroll, Giampaolo D’Alessandro, Gian Luca Lippi, Gian-Luca Oppo, Francesco Papoff
arxiv-2201-02468.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Mark Anthony Carroll, Giampaolo D’Alessandro, Gian Luca Lippi, Gian-Luca Oppo, Francesco Papoff. We deconstruct and address a comment to Carroll et al. [Phys Rev Lett 126, 063902 (2021)] (PRL) that has been posted on arXiv appearing as two versions [arXiv:2106.15242v1] and [arXiv:2106.15242v2]. This comment claimed that a term in the model presented in the PRL had been incorrectly omitted and that, hence, the laser threshold predicted by the model in the PRL is unattainable.

arxiv-2209-01098.title: How Developers Extract Functions: An Experiment Thanks: This research was supported by the ISRAEL SCIENCE FOUNDATION (grant no. 832/18).
arxiv-2209-01098.creator: Alexey Braver Dror G. Feitelson Department of Computer Science The Hebrew University of Jerusalem, Israel
arxiv-2209-01098.description: Abstract Creating functions is at the center of writing computer programs. But there has been little empirical research on how this is done and what are the considerations that developers use. We design an experiment in which we can compare the decisions made by multiple developers under exactly the same conditions.

arxiv-2302-02044.title: Neutron capture-induced silicon nuclear recoils for dark matter and CEνNS Preprint: August 10, 2026
arxiv-2302-02044.creator: K. Harris, A. Gevorgian, A.J. Biffl, A.N. Villano
arxiv-2302-02044.description: Abstract Following neutron capture in a material, there will be prompt nuclear recoils in addition to the gamma cascade. The nuclear recoils that are left behind in materials are generally below 1 keV and therefore in the range of interest for dark matter experiments and CEνNS studies — both as backgrounds and calibration opportunities.

arxiv-2302-03656.title: Revealing the Impact of SIC in NOMA-ISAC
arxiv-2302-03656.creator: Chongjun Ouyang, Yuanwei Liu, Hongwen Yang
arxiv-2302-03656.description: Abstract The impact of successive interference cancellation (SIC) in non-orthogonal multiple access integrated sensing and communications (NOMA-ISAC) is analyzed. A two-stage SIC-based framework is proposed to deal with the inter-communication user and inter-functionality interferences. The performance of sensing and communications (S&C) is analyzed for two SIC orders, i.e., the communications-centric SIC and the sensing-centric SIC.

arxiv-2302-05162.title: Phenomenological model of supercooled liquid as a possible resolution of the Kauzmann paradox
arxiv-2302-05162.creator: M. V. Kondrin, Y.B. Lebed, A.A. Pronin, V.V. Brazhkin
arxiv-2302-05162.description: Abstract The diverging relaxation time in approaching hypothetical ideal glass transition is a subject of hot debate. In the current paper we demonstrate, how diverging relaxation time and turning excess entropy to zero (which is an essence of Kauzmann’s paradox) can be avoided, using as an example the model molecular glassformer, propylene carbonate.

arxiv-2307-14752.title: Dynamical theory of single-photon transport through a qubit chain coupled to a one-dimensional nanophotonic waveguide
arxiv-2307-14752.creator: Ya. S. Greenberg, O. A. Chuikin, A. A. Shtygashev, A. G. Moiseev
arxiv-2307-14752.description: Abstract We study the dynamics of a single-photon pulse travelling through a linear qubit chain coupled to continuum modes in a one-dimensional (1D) photonic waveguide. We derive a time-dependent dynamical theory for qubit amplitudes and for transmitted and reflected spectra.

arxiv-2402-04508.title: Properties of the cone of polynomials of fixed degree that preserve nonnegative matrices
arxiv-2402-04508.creator: Jared Brannan, Benjamin J. Clark, Garrett Kepler
arxiv-2402-04508.description: Abstract As was detailed by Loewy and London in [Linear and Multilinear Algebra 6 (1978/79), no. 1, 83–90], the cone of polynomials that preserve the nonnegativity of matrices may play an important role in the solution to the nonnegative inverse eigenvalue problem.

arxiv-2403-14548.title: DINO-Tracker: Taming DINO for Self-Supervised Point Tracking in a Single Video
arxiv-2403-14548.creator: Narek Tumanyan ∗, Assaf Singer ∗, Shai Bagon, Tali Dekel
arxiv-2403-14548.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Narek Tumanyan ∗, Assaf Singer ∗, Shai Bagon, Tali Dekel. We present DINO-Tracker – a new framework for long-term dense tracking in video. The pillar of our approach is combining test-time training on a single video, with the powerful localized semantic features learned by a pre-trained DINO-ViT model. Specifically, our framework simultaneously adopts DINO’s features to fit to the motion observations of the test video, while training a tracker that directly leverages the refined features.

arxiv-2412-12746.title: EmbedFuzz: High Speed Fuzzing through Transplantation CCS: Security and privacy Systems security CCS: Security and privacy Embedded systems security CCS: Computer systems organization Firmware CCS: Computer systems organization Embedded software CCS: Software and its engineering Software testing and
arxiv-2412-12746.creator: Florian Hofhammer, Qinying Wang, Atri Bhattacharyya, Majid Salehi, Bruno Crispo, Manuel Egele, Mathias Payer, Marcel Busch
arxiv-2412-12746.description: Abstract . Dynamic analysis and especially fuzzing are challenging tasks for embedded firmware running on modern low-end MCU due to performance overheads from instruction emulation, the difficulty of emulating the vast space of available peripherals, and low availability of open-source embedded firmware. Consequently, efficient security testing of MCU firmware has proved to be a resource- and engineering-heavy endeavor.

arxiv-2508-18292.title: Consensus Is All You Need: Gossip-Based Reasoning Among Large Language Models
arxiv-2508-18292.creator: Saksham Arora
arxiv-2508-18292.description: Abstract Large language models have advanced rapidly, but no single model excels in every area—each has its strengths and weaknesses. Instead of relying on one model alone, we take inspiration from gossip protocols in distributed systems, where information is exchanged with peers until they all come to an agreement.

arxiv-2602-01008.title: Adapting Where It Matters: Depth-Aware Adaptation for Efficient Multilingual Speech Recognition in Low-Resource Languages
arxiv-2602-01008.creator: Yang Xiao , Eun-Jung Holden , Ting Dang The University of Melbourne

pmc-11450238.title: Public Perceptions of Enuresis: Insights From Online Communities in South Korea and the United States
pmc-11450238.creator: Jung Eun Yu, Kwang Jin Ko, Jung Yoon Kim
pmc-11450238.description: PurposeTo establish a foundation for raising awareness and disseminating accurate information about enuresis—one of the most challenging conditions to discuss openly—this paper examines public perceptions of enuresis.MethodsThis paper collected title and text data from posts related to enuresis on the top popular online platforms such Naver Cafe in South Korea and Reddit in the United States (US).

pmc-11456845.title: Can IFRS adoption mitigate earnings management in an emerging market?
pmc-11456845.creator: Abdelnaser M Mohamed Amer, Asil Azimli, Muri Wole Adedokun
pmc-11456845.description: Research on the impact of the International Financial Reporting Standard (IFRS) mandate on the quality of financial reporting produced mixed findings. Several researchers showed that the IFRS mandate depresses earnings management since it improves comparability, and the principle-based approach offers limited alternatives for managers in reporting.

pmc-11522283.title: Association of albumin-corrected anion gap with severe consciousness disorders and outcomes in ischemic stroke: a retrospective MIMIC analysis
pmc-11522283.creator: Ying Chen, Ming-Yao You, Lan Chu
pmc-11522283.description: The relationship between albumin-corrected anion gap (ACAG) and severe disorder of consciousness (SDOC), in-hospital mortality, and long-term mortality in patients with ischemic stroke (IS) remains unclear. This study investigates the association of ACAG with SDOC and other outcomes in IS using data from the MIMIC-IV database.

pmc-11663748.title: CPAP and inflammation: villain or good guy?
pmc-11663748.creator: Liliane P de Souza Mendes, Rafaela Garcia Santos de Andrade, Rodrigo Pinto Pedrosa, Flávia Baggio Nerbass
pmc-11663748.description: giopoietin-2 (Ang-2) levels compared to those treated with lower pressures.1 Upon closer examination of the results, however, we believe that certain considerations need to be addressed. The authors introduced the topic by referencing two previous randomised clinical trials that failed to demonstrate cardiovascular risk reduction in participants with good CPAP adherence.

pmc-11678793.title: Pharmacodynamic Evaluation of Phage Therapy in Ameliorating ETEC-Induced Diarrhea in Mice Models
pmc-11678793.creator: Yangjing Xiong, Lu Xia, Yumin Zhang, Guoqing Zhao, Shidan Zhang, Jingjiao Ma, Yuqiang Cheng, Hengan Wang, Jianhe Sun, Yaxian Yan, Zhaofei Wang
pmc-11678793.description: Enterotoxigenic Escherichia coli (ETEC) is a major pathogen causing diarrhea in humans and animals, with increasing antimicrobial resistance posing a growing challenge in recent years. Lytic bacteriophages (phages) offer a targeted and environmentally sustainable approach to combating bacterial infections, particularly in eliminating drug-resistant strains.

pmc-11805012.title: Effect of Enamel Surface Coating on Staining Capability Due to Iron-Containing Supplements on Primary Teeth: An in Vitro Study
pmc-11805012.creator: Divya Nasha, Amreen Aijazuddin, Kodali Srija, Mrunal Dave, Prasanta Majumder, Disha Makwani, Poonam Joshi, Sonu Acharya
pmc-11805012.description: Background:The staining of primary teeth due to iron-containing supplements is a common concern among parents and healthcare providers.Materials and Methods:Forty extracted primary teeth were divided into two groups of 20 each. Group A served as the control and received no enamel coating, while Group B was treated with a commercially available enamel surface coating.

pmc-12492701.title: Analysis of the presence of Beta-hemolytic streptococci and cytological profiles in horse tracheal lavage samples with diverse clinical respiratory symptoms
pmc-12492701.creator: Orhan Pınar, Cansu Çelik Doğan, Deniz Aktaran Bala, Cihan Kumaş, Alper Mete
pmc-12492701.description: BackgroundRiding clubs face significant financial losses due to upper respiratory infections caused by Beta-hemolytic (β-hemolytic) streptococci, leading to strangles and related diseases that negatively impact the health and performance of horses. Our objective was to determine the relationship between these inflammatory cells, the presence of β-hemolytic streptococcal species, and the clinical symptoms exhibited by the horses.

pmc-12516571.title: Non-osteoporotic multilevel contiguous vertebral compression: a rare clinical case report
pmc-12516571.creator: Wongthawat Liawrungrueang, Watcharaporn Cholamjiak, Peem Sarasombath
pmc-12516571.description: BackgroundMultiple-level contiguous vertebral compression fractures (VCFs) are typically associated with osteoporosis or pathological conditions. The occurrence of such fractures in individuals with normal bone mineral density following high-energy trauma is exceedingly rare.Case DescriptionWe report the case of a 64-year-old male construction worker who sustained a fall from a height of approximately 4 meters, landing on his feet.

pmc-12838820.title: Generation of Bioactive Stem Cell-Derived Secretome in 3D Bioreactor System: Towards Cell-Free Therapy in Veterinary Medicine
pmc-12838820.creator: Věra Daňková, Andrea Exnerová, Hana Vágnerová, Vojtěch Pavlík, Kristina Nešporová
pmc-12838820.description: Canine adipose-derived mesenchymal stem cells (cASC) are promising for regenerative veterinary medicine due to their immunomodulatory and reparative capacities. Three-dimensional (3D) culturing provides a more physiologically relevant environment than conventional two-dimensional (2D) monolayers, enhancing paracrine activity and therapeutic potential of mesenchymal stem cells (MSC).

pmc-12984033.title: Tracheoesophageal fistula repair with veno-venous extracorporeal support and Montgomery T-tube: a case report
pmc-12984033.creator: José Luis Che Morales, Gary Kosai Vargas Mendoza
pmc-12984033.description: Tracheoesophageal fistulas (TEFs) are a major surgical challenge requiring a meticulous approach. This case report describes the successful surgical treatment of a 50 mm TEF extending from the upper third of the trachea to 40 mm above the main carina in a young female patient.

pmc-13141079.title: Limited impact of autochthonous bioaugmentation used for the bioremediation of the oily desert soil at elevated temperatures
pmc-13141079.creator: Dina M Al-Mailem, Mayada K Kansour
pmc-13141079.description: SummaryTo investigate the potential of autochthonous bioaugmentation to enhance the bioremediation of oil-contaminated soils at high temperatures, pristine Kuwaiti desert soil samples were contaminated with oil and bioaugmented with four autochthonous thermotolerant/thermophilic hydrocarbonoclastic bacteria, individually and as consortia. Even without bioaugmentation, all treated soil samples had similar cultivable communities after bioremediation.

pmc-13179418.title: Monoradicular Primary Maxillary Left Second Molar: A Rare Root Morphology and Review of the Literature
pmc-13179418.creator: Basim Almulhim
pmc-13179418.description: Understanding the anatomical variations between primary and permanent dentitions and familiarity with the internal and external root morphology are essential for dental practitioners to distinguish root morphological anomalies. A search in dental literature reveals the occurrence of monoradicular molars in primary dentition; especially the monoradicular maxillary primary second molar is extremely rare, returning only five case reports.

pmc-13284042.title: Postoperative S100B protein levels as a measure for predicting neurological deficit in children undergoing cardiac surgery
pmc-13284042.creator: Evyatar Hubara, Lital kalich Philosoph, Simon Lassman, Yelena Skourikhin, Rina Hemi, Omer Bar-Yosef
pmc-13284042.description: Brain injury following congenital heart surgery is associated with long-term neurodevelopmental deficits. Early identification of such injury may guide timely neuroprotective interventions. The calcium-binding protein S100B has been established in retrospective studies to be associated with poor neurological outcomes after surgery. These findings suggest that S100B may serve as a biomarker of central nervous system injury.

pmc-13452195.title: Mitochondria-targeted SkQ1 supplementation enhances post-thaw quality, cryosurvival, and functional competence of rooster spermatozoa
pmc-13452195.creator: Ranieh Hadi Hassan, Mohammad Shamsollahi, Mahdieh Mehdipour, Farshid Fatahnia, Yaser Khorram Del
pmc-13452195.description: The present study investigated the effects of different concentrations of SkQ1, a mitochondria-targeted antioxidant, on the post-thaw quality of rooster spermatozoa. Pooled semen samples were diluted in a Lake-based freezing extender containing 0, 12.5, 25, 50, or 100 nM SkQ1 and cryopreserved in liquid nitrogen.

pmc-13455301.title: Perceptions of frailty pathway implementation in an acute setting among healthcare professionals: a qualitative study using the CFIR 2.0
pmc-13455301.creator: Rebecca Hui Shan Ong, Jin Wee Ng, Fuyin Li, Gek Kheng Png, Hong Choon Oh, Kiat Sern Goh, Barbara Helen Rosario
pmc-13455301.description: BackgroundFrailty is prevalent among older inpatients and is associated with poor outcomes. Hospital frailty pathways are structured approaches to identify, assess, and manage frailty in acute care, and can potentially improve patient outcomes, but they require adaptation to the local context for successful implementation.

pmc-13494041.title: Isolation and evaluation of candidate plant-protecting bacteria from rice seedlings asymptomatic to Burkholderia glumae infection
pmc-13494041.creator: Takumi Nagasawa, Masato Takahashi, Chiharu Akimoto-Tomiyama, Hideki Aoyagi
pmc-13494041.description: Burkholderia glumae is a major causal agent of bacterial panicle blight (BPB) in rice, which is characterized by seedling and grain rot. Therefore, the aim of this study was to isolate potential biocontrol bacteria from rice and investigate their efficacies against B. glumae. Potential biocontrol bacteria were isolated from rice seedlings asymptomatic to B.

pmc-13543738.title: Valorization of Zingiber officinale Roscoe leaf biomass: phytotoxic potential and chemical profiling toward sustainable weed management
pmc-13543738.creator: Sara Vitalini, Orlando Innaurato, Shadab Faramarzi, Alessandro Palmioli, Stefania Garzoli, Valentina Vaglia, Cristina Airoldi, Marcello Iriti
pmc-13543738.description: BACKGROUND Zingiber officinale Roscoe is widely cultivated as a spice and functional food, generating substantial amounts of aerial biomass that is commonly discarded after harvest. Within a circular‐economy framework, this study investigated the phytotoxic potential of Z. officinale leaf biomass and its relevance for sustainable agricultural systems.

pmc-13646835.title: A Multicenter Registry for Rare Interstitial Lung Diseases in Korea: Baseline Characteristics and Clinical Outcomes
pmc-13646835.creator: Ju Hyun Oh, Jae Ha Lee, Sung Woo Park, Yong Suk Jo, Jong Sun Park, Hongseok Yoo, Kyung Hoon Kim, Yangin Jegal, Joo Hun Park, Jinkyeong Park, Taehun Kim, Bo-Guen Kim, Hyung Koo Kang, Hyun-Kyung Lee, Ji Young Kang, Hee-Young Yoon, Hye Ju Yeo, Dong Won Park, Ala Woo, Jung-Wan Yoo, Jin Woo Song, on behalf of the Rare ILD Registry investigators

pmc-13650308.title: Redefining Worker Protection in the Algorithmic Era: From Algorithmic Justice to Insurance Systems for the Gig Economy
pmc-13650308.creator: Jian Lee, Jinha Yoon
pmc-13650308.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The rapid expansion of the digital platform economy has introduced novel occupational hazards driven by algorithmic management. This short communication examines the occupational health challenges faced by gig workers in the context of algorithmic control, focusing on four key mechanisms: trade-offs between economic success and worker health, uncertainty in terms of effort and reward, unreliable assessment of job performance, and incorrect attribution of responsibility.
